questions.question_text:
A signal flare is fired from the ground.
Its height $h$ metres after $t$ seconds is modelled by $h=-5t^{2}+40t$, whose $t$-intercepts are $t=0$ and $t=8$.
What is the greatest height the flare reaches?

options.why: Gives the time of the greatest height instead of the height itself.
Reads the coefficient of $t$ as the greatest height rather than substituting into the model.
Gives the time at which the flare lands rather than a height.

questions.solution_text:
The greatest height is at the vertex, midway between the intercepts.
$\frac{0+8}{2}=4$
$h=-5(4)^{2}+40(4)$
$=-80+160$
$=80$
The greatest height is $80$ m.

options.text: The ball is back on the ground $6$ seconds after it is kicked
The ball reaches its greatest height after $6$ seconds
options.why: Confuses an $x$-intercept with the vertex; the greatest height is at $t=3$.

options.text: The ball is $6$ m above the ground
options.why: Reads the value on the horizontal axis as a height rather than a time.

options.text: The ball was kicked from a height of $6$ m
options.why: Describes the vertical intercept, which is the starting height, not the point where the curve returns to the axis.

questions.solution_text:
On the horizontal axis the height is zero.
The curve meets that axis again at $t=6$.
The ball is back on the ground $6$ seconds after it is kicked.

questions.question_text:
A stall's daily profit $P$ dollars from selling $x$ boxes is modelled by $P=-2x^{2}+24x-40$.
What does the $P$-intercept of this model tell you?

options.text: With no boxes sold the stall makes a loss of $\$40$

options.why: Reads the vertical intercept as the maximum; the maximum is at the vertex, not at $x=0$.

options.text: The stall must sell $40$ boxes to make a profit
options.why: Reads a dollar amount on the vertical axis as a number of boxes on the horizontal axis.

options.text: The stall starts the day with a profit of $\$40$
options.why: Ignores the negative sign; the intercept is $-40$, which is a loss.

questions.solution_text:
At $x=0$, $P=-2(0)^{2}+24(0)-40=-40$.
A profit of $-\$40$ is a loss of $\$40$.
Selling no boxes leaves the stall $\$40$ out of pocket, which is its fixed cost for the day.

questions.question_text:
The area $A$ square metres of a garden plot of width $w$ metres is modelled by $A=-0.5w^{2}+16w$.
Find the area when the width is $6$ m.

options.why: Did not square the width, computing $-0.5\times6+16\times6$.
Squared $-0.5w$ instead of $w$, giving $9$ for the first term instead of $-18$.
Lost the negative sign on the squared term, adding $18$ instead of subtracting it.

questions.question_text:
A ball is thrown from a roof.
Its height $h$ metres after $t$ seconds is modelled by $h=-5t^{2}+10t+40$, whose $t$-intercepts are $t=-2$ and $t=4$.
For which values of $t$ does the model make sense?

options.why: Includes negative time, which is before the ball was thrown.
Rules out negative time but lets the model run past the landing, where it gives negative heights.
Stops at the vertex, but the ball keeps falling after it reaches its greatest height.

questions.solution_text:
The ball is thrown at $t=0$, so negative values of $t$ have no meaning.
At $t=4$ the height is zero, which is when the ball lands.
Beyond $t=4$ the model gives negative heights, which would be below the ground.
The model makes sense for $0\le t\le4$.

options.why: Gives the time of the greatest height instead of the two times at the stated height.
Gives only the later crossing; a horizontal line at $h=21$ cuts the curve twice.
Picks two times either side of the vertex without checking the height at each one.

questions.solution_text:
Read across from $h=21$ to the curve, then down to the horizontal axis.
The curve is at $h=21$ when $t=3$ and when $t=7$.
Check: $-(3)^{2}+10(3)=21$ and $-(7)^{2}+10(7)=21$.
The drone is $21$ m above the ground after $3$ seconds and after $7$ seconds.

questions.question_text:
The cost $C$ dollars of making $x$ crates is modelled by $C=x^{2}-10x+40$, whose vertex is $(5,15)$.
What does the vertex tell you?

options.text: The lowest cost is $\$15$, and it happens when $5$ crates are made
The lowest cost is $\$5$, and it happens when $15$ crates are made
options.why: Reads the vertex coordinates in the wrong order, taking the first number as the cost.

options.text: The highest cost is $\$15$, and it happens when $5$ crates are made
options.why: Treats every vertex as a maximum; here the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is positive, so the parabola opens upwards.

options.text: The highest cost is $\$5$, and it happens when $15$ crates are made
options.why: Swaps the vertex coordinates AND calls the turning point of an upward parabola a maximum.

questions.solution_text:
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ is positive, so the parabola opens upwards and the vertex is its lowest point.
The vertex $(5,15)$ has $x=5$ and $C=15$.
The lowest cost is $\$15$, and it happens when $5$ crates are made.

questions.question_text:
A bakery's weekly profit $P$ dollars from selling $n$ cakes is modelled by a parabola with $n$-intercepts at $n=20$ and $n=180$.
What do these two intercepts tell the bakery?

options.text: At $20$ cakes and at $180$ cakes the bakery breaks even, making neither a profit nor a loss
The bakery makes its greatest profit at $20$ cakes and at $180$ cakes
options.why: Confuses the intercepts with the vertex; the greatest profit is midway between them, at $100$ cakes.

options.text: The bakery can sell at most $20$ cakes and at least $180$ cakes
options.why: Treats the intercepts as limits on sales rather than as the points where the profit is zero.

options.text: The bakery makes a profit of $\$20$ and a profit of $\$180$
options.why: Reads values on the horizontal axis as dollar amounts; on the $n$-axis the profit is zero.

questions.solution_text:
An $n$-intercept is a point where $P=0$.
A profit of zero means the money coming in exactly matches the money going out.
At $20$ cakes and at $180$ cakes the bakery breaks even.

questions.question_text:
The height, $h$ metres, of a ball above the ground $t$ seconds after it has been thrown upwards is given by $h=5t-2t^2$.
What is the greatest height the ball reaches above the ground?

options.why: Substitutes an inappropriate time or sign and gives a negative height rather than the vertex value.
Estimates the maximum without evaluating the quadratic at its exact vertex.
Uses a root of the height equation, which is when the ball is on the ground, not at its maximum.
